briefings.title: China Could Have Crushed the U.S. Economy. Why Didn't It?
briefings.tldr: President Xi Jinping’s high-stakes state visit to Washington highlights a strategic stalemate between the U.S. and China, where neither side can deliver a knockout blow, prompting an ongoing debate among experts regarding whether a durable détente or escalating K-shaped competition defines the future of the relationship.

briefings.title: Former U.S. national security advisor Jake Sullivan speaks at CANSEC in Ottawa – May 28, 2026
briefings.tldr: Despite current bilateral frictions and the end of the post-Cold War era, the U.S. and Canada are bound by a "triple destiny" of geography, democracy, and technology.

briefings.title: Why Trump Can't Stand Still: The Iran War He Doesn't Know How to End
briefings.tldr: The Trump administration is reportedly nearing a framework agreement to end the war with Iran and begin a 30-day negotiation period, even as military readiness declines and a diplomatic rift with Germany triggers a significant drawdown of U.S. troops in Europe.

briefings.title: Jake Sullivan: Is America Losing the High Ground? | Foreign Affairs Interview
briefings.tldr: Technological supremacy, particularly in AI and production scale, has become the primary driver of geopolitical power, requiring the U.S. to abandon laissez-faire economics for a modern industrial strategy to counter China’s state-directed model and navigate increasingly volatile global flashpoints.

briefings.title: 'Sheer lack of planning': Jake Sullivan slams WH for not thinking through the consequences of war
briefings.tldr: Former National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan warns that the Trump administration’s "war of choice" against Iran lacks clear strategic objectives and a viable "off-ramp," arguing that tactical military successes have not made the U.S. safer or permanently neutralized the nuclear threat.

briefings.title: Rethinking Risk and Global Power with Jake Sullivan | The Outthinking Investor
briefings.tldr: The world has transitioned from the post-Cold War "unipolar moment" to an "old normal" of great power rivalry where economics and national security are inextricably linked, requiring the U.S. to move beyond punitive measures toward "offensive" economic statecraft like a national strategic investment fund.

briefings.title: Fmr. National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan on China, the U.S. & the AI Race | Amanpour and Company
briefings.tldr: The United States and China are engaged in a high-stakes race for AI supremacy that mirrors the Cold War’s nuclear and space races, requiring the U.S. to balance aggressive private-sector innovation with stringent export controls and sustained diplomatic safety talks.
